title: [Good First Issue]: Align behavior of ONNX Frontend function Relu-6, 13, 14 with original framework
body:
### Context

Neural networks are graphs consisting of nodes called operators. Each operator corresponds to a mathematical function, usually described in framework's documentation or an AI standard, such as ONNX.
OpenVINO ONNX Frontend is a component responsible for working with ONNX graphs and requires implementation of different ONNX operators in order to use ONNX models.
This task requires alignment between OpenVINO ONNX Frontend and original framework implementations of Relu for next list of opsets: [opset 6](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md#Relu-6),  [opset 13](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md#Relu-13),  [opset 14](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md#Relu-14)
Necessary help will be provided by ONNX Fronted team.


### What needs to be done?

Operator details can be found in [ONNX Operators](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Operators.md#Relu)
More details can be found in ONNX Changelog: [opset 6](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md#Relu-6),  [opset 13](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md#Relu-13),  [opset 14](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Changelog.md#Relu-14)
1. Function already has a common implementation in OpenVINO. First of all, you need to review a documentation and prepare a table with differences between versions. It could be, for instance, a missing property, extended/reduced coverage of existing property, etc...
2. Copy existing implementation [here](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/tree/master/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op) to make it aligned with original framework (extend or reduce coverage of a common implementation). Copy of modified implementation should be in a defined opset, or in opset 1 in case it implements oldest implementation. [Example of multi-opset operation](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/op/softmax.cpp#L50).
3. Register the function in [ops_bridge.cpp](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/frontend/src/ops_bridge.cpp#L554-L560) while keeping alphabetical order
4. Create test model(s) in [ONNX models directory](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/tree/master/src/frontends/onnx/tests/models/). OpenVINO test infrastructure then converts prototxt files to ONNX models - you will use those models later in tests
5. Add tests covering all use cases [here](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/tests/onnx_import.in.cpp)
6. Check [Python xfailed tests](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/tests/tests_python/test_backend.py) to find a test marked as a xfailed for added functionality. If any exist - remove corresponding lines and try to verify by using cmdline "python -m pytest -k name_of_test".
More details in [adding operators to ONNX Frontend guide](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/docs/how_to_add_op.md)

comments.body:
I've created test cases and I tried running them with `/bin/intel64/Debug/ov_onnx_frontend_tests --gtest_filter=*onnx_model_relu_*`. @reporter said "OpenVINO test infrastructure then converts prototxt files to ONNX models" but I find no onnx models under "/scratch/chanelsi/openvino/bin/intel64/Debug/./test_model_zoo/onnx/<name>.onnx", which is the path convert_model() in each test in onnx_import.in.cpp is looking for. I understand the . in the path may cause the issue, but there's indeed no converted onnx files in the entire workspace.

Here's my build option (run on build directory):
```
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DENABLE_PYTHON=ON -DENABLE_TESTS=ON -DENABLE_FUNCTIONAL_TESTS=ON -DENABLE_DEBUG_CAPS=ON -DENABLE_CPU_DEBUG_CAPS=ON -DENABLE_NCC_STYLE=ON ..
```

There're no onnx models converted after running `cmake --build . --parallel`

Hello, I too faced the same issue one point in time, but I found the solution. It's quite a simple fix. 
It's simply because you haven't installed the python packages needed for generating ONNX models.
___
There is a [requirements.txt](https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/blob/master/src/frontends/onnx/tests/requirements.txt) in `<project-dir>/src/frontends/onnx/tests`. 
Use pip to install the requirements `pip install -r requirements.txt` in your preferred manner.
And next time you run the build, `.onnx` files will be generated.

Hope this solves your issue
